verdict.rationale: Baseten documents asynchronous inference on deployed models. It returns a request ID and completes later via webhook or polling, and the docs say this suits batch work. However, no evidence shows async or batch requests are priced at a discount to real-time; the only documented discount is for cached input tokens, which is a separate feature. Missing for 10: a documented batch or async pricing discount versus real-time rates, a dedicated batch-job submission API (e.g. file-based bulk jobs), and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can submit asynchronous batch inference jobs at a documented discount versus real-time pricing

citations.quote: Async inference returns a request ID quickly and completes later through webhook or polling, which suits batch work, long documents, or any case where the caller should not hold a connection open for minutes.
